blocks.label: Bridge
blocks.note: Four weeks back into triathlon: the Arc's week at lower volume, all Zone 2, three swims a week.

blocks.label: Arc
blocks.note: The 26-week build to the race: base, build, race-specific, taper.

mon.title: Technique swim
mon.effort: Easy throughout. Technique is the point, not the distance.
setLines: 8 × 50 drill - 20s rest (rotate: fingertip drag, catch-up, single-arm, 6-3-6)
detail: First thing, then strength in the same trip. Swim frequency is the cheapest speed a newer swimmer can buy.
Pick ONE cue for the whole session.

mon.title: Strength
mon.effort: RPE 7 - two or three reps in the tank, nothing to failure. A shorter session drops one set from every lift.
setLines: Calf Raises 3×15 - straight knee, then bent knee
detail: Straight after the swim.
Heavy and low-volume keeps the strength without adding size. Weight is decided in the kitchen, not here.

mon.title: Lunch run
mon.effort: Zone 2 - easy. Short on purpose.
detail: The day after the long run, this loosens you up. Do not extend it.

tue.title: {tueTitle}
detail: No trainer yet? A gym bike works - same time, same effort - but 45 minutes is the most that fits there before 7:45.
Outdoors only in daylight.

wed.title: Main swim
wed.effort: Steady - the last rep at the same pace as the first.
detail: Short on purpose: Wednesday is a work day and the pool opens at 6, so 45 minutes in the water is the most it holds.
Count strokes per length on the main set.
If the count climbs more than 3-4 from first rep to last, the stroke is falling apart - note when.

Warm up 10-15 min easy before any efforts; spin easy to the full time.

fuel.longRide: 60-75g carb/hr, starting at 30 min. Start using the products you plan to race with.
fuel.longRun: Water for the first hour, then 30-45g carb/hr.

mon.title: Strength

setLines: Calf Raises 3×15 - straight knee, then bent knee
detail: Straight after the swim.
If Tuesday's intervals suffer, move the squats and RDLs to Tuesday, after the ride.

mon.title: Lunch run
mon.effort: Zone 2 - easy. Short on purpose.
detail: The day after the long run, this loosens you up. Do not extend it.

tue.title: {tueTitle}
detail: Zone 4 is 88-95% FTP - ERG mode on the trainer holds it for you. By heart rate it is 83-89% max, but bike HR runs 5-10 bpm low, so trust RPE 7.
Warm up 15 min easy, building, before the first interval; spin easy to the full time.

wed.title: Main swim
wed.effort: Steady sets hold the same pace on the last rep as the first. CSS is your pace per 100 m from the last test.
detail: Short on purpose: Wednesday is a work day and the pool opens at 6, so 45 minutes in the water is the most it holds.
Count strokes per length on the main set.
If the count climbs more than 3-4 from first rep to last, the stroke is falling apart - note when.

thu.title: {thuTitle}
detail: Zone 4 is 83-89% max HR, or just under the HR from your last run test. Even effort: the last rep looks like the first.
Warm up 15 min easy before the first interval; jog easy to the full time.

fri.title: Aerobic swim
fri.effort: Steady and continuous - the long swim of the week. Steady, not hard: the big weekend comes next.
detail: Non-stop means non-stop: slow down rather than stop.
Friday is a home day, so it is the morning with time for the long swim.

sat.title: Long ride
detail: The anchor session of the week. Put the Zone 3 blocks in the middle hours, not the first.
Hawi is a long climb into the wind: if you have hills, put the Zone 3 blocks on them. Indoors, set a 2-4% grade.
Build time in the aero position: 10-minute blocks, working toward 30 and more.
Indoors: if it has to shrink, keep the Zone 3 work and cut the easy tail.

sat.title: Brick run
sat.effort: Easy - short, quick steps for the first 5 min. Wooden legs are normal and pass.
detail: Running within 5 minutes of getting off the bike. That transition is the whole point.

sun.title: Long run
detail: Run it by effort, not pace.

fuel.longRide: 75-90g carb/hr from 30 min - the exact products you'll race with. This is gut training; build up to it.
fuel.longRun: 30-45g carb/hr - a gel every 30-40 min, as on race day.

mon.title: Technique swim
mon.effort: Easy throughout. Technique is the point, not the distance.
setLines: 8 × 50 drill - 20s rest (rotate: fingertip drag, catch-up, single-arm, 6-3-6)
detail: First thing, then strength in the same trip. Swim frequency is the cheapest speed a newer swimmer can buy.
Pick ONE cue for the whole session.

mon.title: Strength
mon.effort: RPE 6 - crisp, fast reps. Nothing heavy, nothing to failure.
detail: Straight after the swim.
Recovery week: one set of each, and call it done.

mon.title: Lunch run
mon.effort: Zone 2 - easy. Short on purpose.
detail: The day after the long run, this loosens you up. Do not extend it.

tue.title: {tueTitle}
detail: Zone 4 is 88-95% FTP; race effort is 70-75% FTP, RPE 5. Bike HR runs 5-10 bpm low - trust power, then RPE.
Warm up 15 min easy, building, before the first interval; spin easy to the full time.

wed.title: Main swim
wed.effort: Race effort is CSS+5 to +8 per 100 m - steady enough to breathe every 2-3 strokes the whole way.
detail: Short on purpose: Wednesday is a work day and the pool opens at 6, so 45 minutes in the water is the most it holds.
Sight on the main set: lift your eyes forward every 6th stroke, crocodile-style, without lifting your head.

thu.title: {thuTitle}
detail: Race effort is what you could hold for about two hours fresh - mid Zone 3, RPE 6. On race day you hold it after three hours on the bike.
Warm up 10-15 min easy first; jog easy to the full time.

fri.title: Aerobic swim
fri.effort: The long swim of the week. Race effort is CSS+5 to +8 per 100 m; sight as you go.
detail: Friday is a home day, so it is the morning with time for the long swim. The race-distance swims live here.
Open water: never alone, and with a tow float.
Race day in Hawaii is almost certainly non-wetsuit, so pool swimming is race-specific swimming.

sat.title: Long ride
detail: Race-effort blocks go exactly as you'll race: aero position, race nutrition, race kit when you can.
Put race effort on climbs and into headwinds when you can - that is the road to Hawi. Indoor apps such as Rouvy have the actual 70.3 Hawaii course.
Indoors: if it has to shrink, keep the race-effort work and cut the easy tail.

sat.title: Brick run
detail: Running within 5 minutes of getting off the bike.
Practise race-run fuelling on the longer ones: a gel at 20-30 min.

sun.title: Long run
detail: Run it by effort, not pace. The day after a big Saturday the pace will be slow - that is the point.
Put some of it on grass or trail: the race run crosses golf-course fairways and lava-field paths.

fuel.longRide: 75-90g carb/hr from 30 min - the exact products you'll race with. This is gut training; build up to it.
fuel.longRun: 30-45g carb/hr - a gel every 30-40 min, as on race day.

mon.title: Technique swim
mon.effort: Easy throughout. Technique is the point, not the distance.
setLines: 8 × 50 drill - 20s rest (rotate: fingertip drag, catch-up, single-arm, 6-3-6)
detail: Optional this week.
Pick ONE cue for the whole session.

mon.title: Strength
mon.effort: Bodyweight only - two rounds, nothing hard. This is staying loose, not training.
detail: After the swim, or at home if you skip it.

mon.title: Lunch run
mon.effort: Zone 2 - easy. Short on purpose.
detail: Do not extend it.

tue.title: Race-effort bike
tue.effort: 3 × 8 min at race effort - 70-75% FTP, RPE 5. 4 min easy between.
detail: Taper: the volume drops, the intensity doesn't. Feeling flat or twitchy this week is normal.
Heat block: no fan, dress warm, then 20-30 min in a sauna or hot bath. Start shorter if it's new to you, drink before and after, and get out if you feel dizzy.

wed.title: Main swim
wed.effort: Race effort - CSS+5 to +8 per 100 m. Sharp, not tired.

thu.title: Race-effort run
thu.effort: 3 × 6 min at race effort - mid Zone 3, RPE 6. 2 min jog between.
detail: Warm up 10-15 min easy first; jog easy to the full time.
Heat block: overdress - long sleeves and a hat - then the sauna or hot bath.

fri.title: Aerobic swim
fri.effort: Easy, with a little speed at the end.
setLines: MAIN SET: 5 × 100 easy-steady, then 4 × 50 fast - 20s rest
detail: Open water if you can get it, never alone.

sat.title: Long ride
sat.effort: 2 × 15 min race effort - inside a Zone 2 ride, 70-75% FTP, RPE 5.
detail: The last ride with any length to it. Race kit, race nutrition.

sat.title: Brick run
sat.effort: First 10 min at race effort, then easy.
detail: Running within 5 minutes of getting off the bike.

sun.title: Long run
sun.effort: Zone 2 with 4 × 3 min at race effort - 2 min easy between.
detail: Run it by effort, not pace.
Pack tonight for tomorrow's flight: bike case, race kit, nutrition, sunscreen.

fuel.longRide: Race: 60-90g carb/hr - whatever you trained - with 500-750ml fluid/hr and electrolytes. In Hawaii heat, plan on the top of that fluid range. Eat every 20 min on a timer.
fuel.longRun: Race: a gel or on-course carbs every ~30 min. Water and ice at every aid station.

mon.title: Travel day
mon.effort: Fly to Kona (KOA). Walk or jog 15 min easy after the flight to loosen up.
detail: Memorial Day.
Hawaii is 6 hours behind US Eastern time, so an early-morning race start will feel like midday at home. The time change is on your side.

tue.title: Openers
tue.effort: 3 × 3 min at race effort - 3 min easy between, then spin easy.
detail: Short and sharp. You are reminding your legs, not training them.
Build the bike first and check every gear. Ride part of the course if you can, and feel the wind before Saturday.

wed.title: Main swim
wed.effort: Race effort on the 100s, easy everything else.
detail: In the ocean at the race venue if you can: sight off the buoys and get used to salt water and chop.

thu.title: Shakeout run
detail: Athlete check-in.
Carb load starts today.

fri.title: Shakeout ride
fri.effort: Easy - 20 min with 3 × 1 min at race effort.
detail: Bike check-in. Then feet up, in the shade.

fri.title: Venue swim
fri.effort: Easy - a few minutes in the race water, if the venue allows it.

sat.title: Race swim
sat.effort: Steady, not hard - start at the side or back of your wave. Sight every 6-8 strokes.
detail: Ocean, almost certainly no wetsuit: a swimskin or just your tri suit.
Sub-7 budget: about 47 min. The effort matters; the clock doesn't.

sat.title: Race bike
sat.effort: Race effort and no higher - the low end, about 70% FTP, in this heat. Ride the first 20 min easy.
detail: The climb to Hawi is long and into the wind: hold the power and let the speed go. You get it back on the way down.
If you're passing people on the climbs, you're riding too hard.
Eat every 20 minutes, on a timer. Drink to the top of your range, with salt.
Sub-7 budget: about 3:28.

sat.title: Race run
sat.effort: Ease into it - the first 5 km at the bottom of race effort. It will feel too easy; then settle in.
detail: Heat decides this leg: ice in your hat and tri suit, a sponge and a drink at every aid station.
Walk the aid stations if that's what it takes to cool down, eat and drink.
Sub-7 budget: about 2:28. Sub-7 is the sum of the legs, not a target for any one of them.

arc.satEffort: RACE REHEARSAL - 3 hours at race effort on the hilliest route you have, then straight into the run. Race breakfast 3 h before, race kit, race nutrition - everything you'll use on June 5.
arc.brickEffort: First 30 min at race effort, then easy.
arc.sunEffort: Easy - Zone 1-2, the day after the rehearsal. Walk breaks are fine.

arc.tueEffort: 3 × 10 min at race effort - 70-75% FTP, RPE 5 - then 4 × 1 min fast. 3 min easy between. The heat block starts today: no fan, dress warm, then 20-30 min in a sauna or hot bath.
arc.thuEffort: 2 × 15 min at race effort - mid Zone 3, RPE 6. 3 min jog between. Overdress for it - long sleeves and a hat.
arc.friMain: 1,300 non-stop with sighting - or 40 min continuous in open water, if it's 16°C/60°F or warmer. A wetsuit at home is for warmth; race day will almost certainly be without one. Never alone.
arc.satEffort: 2 × 30 min race effort - inside a Zone 2 ride, 70-75% FTP, RPE 5.
arc.brickEffort: First 15 min at race effort, then easy.
arc.sunEffort: Zone 2. The last long run - nothing to prove.

cues.name: Exhale, don't hold
cues.detail: Steady bubbles the whole time your face is in the water. Breath-holding is what causes the panic-breathing spiral.

cues.name: Look down
cues.detail: Eyes at the bottom of the pool, slight pressure through the chest. Head lifts as you tire, hips sink, drag.

cues.name: Long in front
cues.detail: Reach, brief glide, finish past the hip. Tired means shortening and spinning the arms.

cues.name: Quiet legs
cues.detail: Small kick from the hip. The kick's job is body position, not propulsion.

big.label: Big day
big.approach: Maintenance or slightly above. Fuel during the session.

moderate.label: Moderate day
moderate.approach: ~300-400 kcal deficit. Carbs concentrated around training.

low.label: Low day
low.approach: ~500 kcal deficit. Protein high, carbs lower.

key.label: Quality day
key.approach: Maintenance calories. Carbs before and after the session - intervals run on glycogen. No deficit today.

maintain.label: Maintenance day
maintain.approach: Maintenance calories, no deficit. Weight should hold steady from here to race day.

carbLoad.label: Carb load
carbLoad.approach: 7-10g carb per kg bodyweight. Cut fibre and fat so it fits. Nothing new.

race.label: Race day
race.approach: Breakfast about 3 hours before the start: 1-2g carb per kg, food you've eaten before every long ride. Then the plan you rehearsed. Nothing new today.

nonNegotiables: Protein 1.6-2.0 g/kg bodyweight, in 3-4 feedings of 25-40g.
Water throughout, plus replacing session losses.
Cap alcohol, especially Friday and Saturday.

fuel.longRun: Water for the first hour, then 20-30g carb/hr.
fuel.post: After the long ride, the long run or a brick: ~1g carb/kg + 25-30g protein within an hour. After anything else, just the next normal meal - no extra recovery snack.
fuel.beforeShort: Water, or a small snack if you're hungry.
fuel.beforeLong: 30-50g carbs before you leave: a banana, or toast with honey.

nutrition.weight: 175 → 165 lb at about ½ lb a week: around 169 by the end of January, 166 by the end of March, then hold. Go by the weekly average, not the day. Losing more than 1 lb a week, or sessions feel flat? Eat more, carbs first. The deficit comes from meals away from training, never from session fuel.

schedule.note: When and where the weekday sessions happen, and what that costs in sleep. Alarm = ready-by time minus the session and everything around it, rounded down to 5 minutes.

trainer.label: Trainer
items: Bike on the trainer, tyres pumped
Fan, towel and a full bottle

run.label: Run
items: Headlamp and reflective vest while it's dark

longRide.label: Long ride
items: Carbs for the whole ride, counted out (see Fuelling)
Outdoors: lights, a spare tube and a pump

brick.label: Brick
items: Running shoes next to the bike

longRun.label: Long run
items: Water, and carbs for past the first hour
